rows.sentence: Here are the steps from the document as executable bullet points:
rows.label: no_rad
rows.rationale: This introduces the list and describes its format.

rows.sentence: **Start on the Adventure Screen.**
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document identifies the Adventure Screen as the starting screen.

rows.sentence: "What you will see first is the Adventure Screen."
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document states this directly.

rows.sentence: The world map is in the upper-right corner, and unexplored areas are black: "until you send a hero to explore an area you won't know what is there".
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document gives the map's location and explains that the black areas have not yet been explored.

rows.sentence: **Confirm your hero is selected.**
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: This check follows from the document's statement that the starting hero should already be selected.

rows.sentence: "Your first hero, Lord Haart, should already be selected".
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document names Lord Haart as the first hero and says he should already be selected.

rows.sentence: **Aim at the town entrance.**
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document directs the player to move the cursor over the town entrance.

rows.sentence: "place your mouse cursor over the entrance to the town (between the two flag poles)"; the horse icon rearing up means the hero will interact with that location.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document gives the cursor location and explains what the rearing horse icon means.

rows.sentence: **Click the location to set the path.**
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document explains that the first click selects the path.

rows.sentence: "a set of green arrows show the path your hero will take to reach the large green X", and the X "marks your hero's destination".
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document confirms what the green arrows and the green X indicate.

rows.sentence: **Click the same location again (or double-click) to send the hero.**
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document describes both a second click and a double-click as ways to send the hero.

rows.sentence: "Click again on the same location and your hero will move to the castle".
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document says that clicking the location again moves the hero to the castle.

rows.sentence: **Wait for the Town Screen.**
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The Town Screen opens when the hero reaches the entrance, without another action.

rows.sentence: "When the hero arrives at the entrance to the town, the view will change to the Town Screen."
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document directly states what triggers the screen change.

rows.sentence: **Check the town info in the bottom-left corner**, which shows "town income (per day) and troop production (per week)"; the top row of boxes is the garrison, the bottom row is troops visiting with a hero.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document confirms the location and contents of the town information and the purpose of both rows.

rows.sentence: **Build a Fort:** "click on the larger of the two buildings on the left side of the town view – the Town Hall – to enter the Hall Screen".
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document gives this as the first step toward building a Fort.

rows.sentence: **Read the building color codes on the Hall Screen:** "Any building you can currently build is shown with its name in a green bar"; "Any building that you can not build, but can be built later is shown with its name in a red bar"; "If a building has been disabled or can never be built, its name will appear in a gray bar"; "Once you have completely built or upgraded a structure as high as it will go, its name will be displayed in gold".
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document gives all four colors and their corresponding building statuses.

rows.sentence: **Build the Fort:** "Click on the picture of the Fort" to see its description and required resources, then "Click on the Build button (in the lower left hand corner of the popup window) and the Fort will be constructed."
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document confirms what clicking the Fort picture reveals and how to construct the Fort.

rows.sentence: **Inspect the Castle Window:** "click on it to view the Castle Window", which "shows you information about all seven units that can be produced by this town"; built Creature Generators (currently the Guardhouse, Archers' Tower, and Barracks) show units available.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document explains how to open the window, what it covers, and which generators currently show available units.

rows.sentence: Click Exit (lower right) to return to the Town Screen.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document specifies the Exit button's location and the screen it returns to.

rows.sentence: **Buy a spell book at the Mage Guild** (the round tower on the right): "All heroes must have a spell book before they can learn or cast spells."
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document locates the Mage Guild, instructs the player to buy a spell book there, and gives the requirement for learning or casting spells.

rows.sentence: **Browse spells on the Mage Guild Screen:** "Left or right clicking on any spell scroll will show you a description of that spell."
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document places the spell scrolls on the Mage Guild Screen and confirms that either click opens a description.

rows.sentence: Click Exit (lower right) to leave.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The Mage Guild instructions identify the lower-right Exit button as the way to leave.

rows.sentence: **Recruit troops:** "Click on the large central tower.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document directs the player to the large central tower to begin recruiting.

rows.sentence: The Recruit Pikemen window is displayed."
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document names the window that opens after clicking the tower.

rows.sentence: **Choose the quantity:** use the scroll bar to select a number (total cost is calculated to the right), or "the fastest way to buy troops is to use the Maximum button (the four up arrows at the bottom of the popup window)", which buys the maximum you can afford.
rows.label: contradictory
rows.rationale: The scroll-bar instructions are correct, but Maximum calculates the affordable quantity; the separate Recruit button completes the purchase.

rows.sentence: **Confirm the purchase:** "Click the Maximum button, then click the Recruit button (bottom center).
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document gives this button sequence and locates the Recruit button at the bottom center.

rows.sentence: Notice how there are now Pikemen in the garrison row of your town."
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The document confirms that the recruited Pikemen appear in the garrison row.
